shipped.title: Interview first, then the old VBW 1 folder

requirements.text: Two consent grants made at the same time from different worktrees of one clone are both kept
A vbw command interrupted mid-commit leaves no stray index files in .vbw/runtime and keeps the caller's own exit cleanup
vbw report and vbw rtk do what their help says
In a real session, a documentation requirement is built by the Docs agent and proved
In a real session, QA fails a phase whose build deviates from its plan, and the fix loop closes it
In balanced autonomy, a background QA run causes no Stop-hook errors and the session reaches the accept stop
Blocking or resetting a plan (its note or status) never withdraws the user's approval of an unchanged contract
Accepting a [human] requirement closes only the fixes opened by the user's own rejections; a fix QA opened stays open until QA passes the phase again
QA cannot record a verdict on a proof older than the current code: vbw qa record refuses and asks for vbw prove first
While one session's VBW run is open, vbw next in another session says the run belongs to another session and to wait or check status; it never tells that session to end the run
vbw run end from a session that does not own the open run is refused, unless the user states that the owning session is closed or the run is older than 24 hours
While a run is open, another session, neither its main conversation nor its agents, can edit the files that run is writing
Turning on autonomous mode in one session leaves it on in every other session where it was on

tools/baseline holds the plan's seven benchmark cases (fix-oneshot, failing-check fix, brownfield feature, safety-destructive, safety-secret, hostile-repo, markdown deliverable), each with a deterministic pass/fail check that fails on the untouched starting project and passes on a correct solution
The benchmark has run every case 3 times with plain Claude Code and 3 times with VBW 2, on Sonnet 5.5 and on Opus 5.5, and its committed results record each run's pass or fail, tokens and cost
docs/benchmark.md compares VBW 2 with plain Claude Code case by case, shows VBW 1 from its recorded runs and behaviour ledger, and states plainly what was not measured
README.md presents VBW 2 to someone new: what it does and why, how to install it, a first project, the commands, with images
CONTRIBUTING.md and the repository's other contributor files describe VBW 2 only: every command, path and tool they name exists

Before planning finishes, every phase has a rigor tier (express, standard or deep) with its reasons, computed from measured signals (requirement count, planned files and size, risk paths, proven requirements it could break, test coverage), and the approval shows each phase's tier and reasons in one line

A phase whose signals call for a higher tier (a risk path such as sign-in, payments, data migrations, secrets, deletion or CI, or many requirements) is never planned below that tier: the Architect may only raise a tier, never lower it
An express phase is approved in one step (its requirement, check and plan together), built by one Dev and proved, and runs QA only when a requirement needs a person's judgement or the phase escalated

While a phase runs, VBW raises its tier on its own and records and shows why when a Dev blocks, a fix needs a second round, QA finds a problem in an express phase, the change touches a risk path or grows well beyond its plan, or a proven requirement fails; it never lowers a tier during a run
Which agents run, how many, the QA tier and the models follow each phase's tier through the profile
The tier is chosen automatically by default; the user can force it with vbw config rigor auto, express, standard or deep

Each finished phase records its predicted tier and the outcome (fix rounds, QA findings, escalations), and vbw show reports how often the prediction held; cost is measured per session by the benchmark
On the seven single-task benchmark cases, VBW 2 with automatic rigor passes every case and costs at most twice what plain Claude Code costs, on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5

The benchmark adds at least three multi-requirement projects (a feature on an existing codebase with earlier requirements to protect, a data migration, and a third non-UI project of several requirements), each graded by a deterministic check, run with plain Claude Code and VBW 2, and docs/benchmark.md reports them plainly

Before approval, every [auto] requirement lists the rules its text states (each condition, edge and error case), each with the check that tests it; vbw apply refuses a listed rule that no check tests, naming it, and the approval screen shows the rules with their checks

vbw prove runs the checks and project commands on a clean copy of the committed code, so uncommitted changes and untracked files in the working folder change no proof result; vbw check keeps running on the working folder for the Dev's red and green steps

A VBW that opens a project record written by a newer VBW says the project needs a newer VBW and how to update, instead of calling the record corrupt, and every VBW still reads the records of older versions

A real-user scenario in tools/l3-suite.sh shows both in the real Claude Code app: a request that states an edge case gets a check for that edge before approval, and a leftover untracked file in the working folder does not change the proof
In every profile and rigor tier, QA agents run on Sonnet or a stronger model, never Haiku; other roles keep the models their profile gives them

rules.text: no profile and no tier cell (quality, balanced, budget x express, standard, deep) gives QA haiku in the tables or in vbw next --json
the budget profile shows QA as Sonnet in config models and the status line
other roles keep their models (budget scout haiku, express dev haiku, quality and balanced unchanged)
a record already holding a haiku QA override (including a model id containing haiku) gets sonnet in next output, no failure
a QA override to opus or a full non-Haiku id is honoured and the dev override still wins
a forced rigor and an escalated or automatic tier never lower QA below Sonnet
the status line shows the same effective QA model the workflow receives
docs and the config skill say QA never uses Haiku

requirements.text: vbw config set model.qa refuses a model weaker than Sonnet (haiku) and says QA needs Sonnet or stronger; sonnet, opus and default are still accepted

rules.text: model.qa haiku exits non-zero with a message that QA needs Sonnet or stronger and leaves the record unchanged
any value naming Haiku, in any case, is refused for model.qa
sonnet, opus, default and a non-Haiku full id are still accepted; default removes the override
the other roles still accept haiku
a refused set writes nothing and keeps an existing valid model.qa override
the config header and skill document the restriction and the kernel stays within 3,000 lines

requirements.text: At the start of a project (after mapping, for existing code), VBW asks three fixed questions: how much software the user has built (never, small scripts or no-code, professionally, senior engineer), how VBW should explain things (plain words, plain with technical terms explained, technical and brief), and how involved they want to be in technical decisions (decide and tell me, options with a recommendation, I make the calls); then what they are building and for whom; then up to three follow-up questions VBW writes for that user and project

rules.text: the three fixed questions are asked in order with exactly the listed options for level, explanation depth and involvement
for an existing codebase the interview comes after mapping, before spec work
after the three, VBW asks briefly what is being built and for whom and writes it into the spec Goals
at most three follow-up questions are asked: zero is allowed, four never
follow-up questions are written for the user's level and this project
the last question asks where to keep the personal answers and applies the choice through the kernel
an unrecognised answer to a fixed question is re-asked or defaulted and never recorded as an invalid value
an interrupted interview records nothing as complete and resumes at the first unanswered question
the router stays within its token budget and the interview within a mode prompt's

requirements.text: The interview's answers are kept in the project, shown by vbw status, asked only once per project (a project started before this version is asked once, at its next milestone), and can be changed later with /vbw:profile

rules.text: a kernel command records level, explanation depth and involvement, and refuses any other value naming the allowed ones
private answers live in the clone's git directory beside consent.json and are never committed or written to the project
shared answers are written to the project record only through the kernel, and choosing one location leaves no copy in the other
private answers in one worktree are read in another worktree of the clone, and concurrent writes are both kept
answers shared by choice are visible to a second worktree of the clone
vbw status shows the three answers and where they are kept, and with none says the interview has not been done
changing one answer later with /vbw:profile leaves the other two untouched and vbw status shows the new value
a record or answers file from an older VBW (no answers) is read without error and counts as not yet interviewed
the record change stays readable by older VBWs (schema 1, under project) and a bad stored value is corrupt
what is being built and for whom is not stored as a personal answer
the interview is asked at a new project's spec step and never again once answers exist, in any session, location or milestone
a project started before this version is asked once, at its next milestone's spec step, and never in the middle of a run or phase

requirements.text: Every VBW step that talks to the user, and every agent whose words reach the user, receives the user's level, explanation depth and involvement, and writes at that level

rules.text: vbw next --json carries the user's level, explanation depth and involvement, with an explicit neutral default when absent
machine-read output is unchanged by the user's level
every skill that speaks to the user receives and applies the three values, and none is skipped
every agent that can reach the user receives and applies the three values
involvement is honored with each of its three settings, including the Architect's decision job
workflow agent calls carry the profile in their task text and still pass a schema
prompts, the router and the workflows stay within their budgets

requirements.text: When VBW proposes requirements and when it presents a plan for approval, it offers at most three suggestions matched to the user's level, each one a yes or no the user may decline; an accepted one becomes a requirement or a recorded decision, and a declined one is not offered again in that project

rules.text: at most three suggestions are offered at a time, each a single yes or no the user may decline, none required to approve
suggestions are offered only at spec proposal and at plan approval, never mid-run or mid-build
an accepted suggestion becomes a requirement or a recorded decision
a declined suggestion is recorded in the project and never offered again, across sessions and milestones
declining identical text twice is deduplicated, even with other case or spacing
suggestion wording follows the user's level and depth, and a project with no answers gets the neutral default
when there is nothing worth suggesting none are shown, and a suggestion never duplicates a requirement or a recorded decision
declined suggestions are written only through the kernel's validated write path and an older record means none declined

requirements.text: A vibe coder and a senior engineer each find VBW's wording right for their level: never too simple, never too technical
Real-user scenarios answer the interview as a newcomer and as a senior engineer; both record their answers, are not asked again, and reach the ship step

rules.text: a newcomer scenario in the real app answers the three fixed questions, what and for whom, the follow-ups and where to keep the answers
a senior-engineer scenario in the real app answers the same questions
both scenarios record their answers, and the recorded answers match what was answered
in both scenarios a second request in a new session does not ask the interview again
both scenarios reach the ship step
the two scenarios record different explanation depth and involvement and save their transcripts for comparison

requirements.text: Closing a fix does not rerun a check that already passed on the same project files under the same approved contract: it says the check is unchanged since its pass, and when that pass was; vbw prove still runs every check

rules.text: after a check passes the record keeps the pass with the file fingerprint, the contract hash and the time
vbw fix done does not run a check whose recorded pass has the same file fingerprint and contract hash, and says it is unchanged since its pass with the date of that pass
a committed change to a served file reruns the check
a changed contract hash reruns the check
a check whose last result was fail or timeout, or that never ran, is rerun, never skipped
a check with no declared files, or whose served files cannot be fingerprinted, is always rerun
uncommitted changes in the fix's files still block closing, and the skip applies only to the check rerun
vbw prove runs every check regardless of recorded passes, and a failing check still fails the proof
a failure of a rerun check still blocks the fix with the same message naming the check
a record without recorded passes reads fine and the new field is validated by the record writer
fix closing outcomes (fixed, or closed for a human requirement) are the same when checks are skipped
the docs describe the reuse rule and its wording, and the kernel stays within its line budget

requirements.text: Several fixes close in one command (vbw fix done F8 F9 F5), running the checks their files serve once; each fix ends as it would if closed alone; a fix that cannot close is named, and the others still close

rules.text: vbw fix done accepts one or more ids, a single id behaves as before, and vbw fix retry still takes exactly one
a check served by several of the named fixes runs once in the command
each fix ends as if closed alone: fixed for code, closed with its requirement returning to the user for a human requirement
a fix that cannot close (unknown id, not open, uncommitted changes, a served check fails) is named with its reason and the others still close
a failing check fails only the fixes it serves, and is named
the same id twice is closed once without error; the exit code is non-zero only if some fix could not close
unchanged earlier passes are still reported as unchanged since their pass, and alone checks still run alone
a partial success leaves the record consistent: closed fixes recorded, unclosed fixes unchanged
fix ids from different requirements and phases mix freely
help text, agent and docs show the multi-id form, and the kernel stays within its line budget

requirements.text: A check the contract marks to run alone (for example one that starts containers) never runs at the same time as another VBW check in the same project, even when several fixes or builds run checks in parallel

rules.text: vbw apply accepts an alone marker on a check
a non-boolean alone value is refused naming the check
the alone marker is part of the contract hash, so adding or removing it needs re-approval
vbw show contract and the approval screen show the marker
an alone check and another check started together in one project never overlap
an alone check waits for running non-alone checks, and non-alone checks wait while an alone check runs
non-alone checks still run in parallel with each other
the exclusion holds across vbw check, vbw prove and the checks run by vbw fix done
a check that times out while holding the exclusion releases it
a crashed vbw process leaves no stale lock: a lock owned by a dead process is taken over
a wait beyond the bounded limit fails with a message naming the check waited on, not a hang
checks of two different projects do not block each other
lock files live under .vbw/runtime and nothing is written outside the project or in /tmp
without an alone marker behaviour and timing are unchanged
the docs describe the alone marker
the kernel stays within its line budget, bash 3.2 compatible, with no eval and no /tmp

requirements.text: A record written by this VBW is either read by VBW 2.0.16 or makes it say the project needs a newer VBW; it is never reported as corrupt

rules.text: closing a fix, proving and keeping the interview answers in the project leave a schema-1 record holding only fields VBW 2.0.16 reads
a field VBW 2.0.16 does not read (alone) raises the schema instead of staying at schema 1
a record carrying passes is refused as corrupt

requirements.text: After a round of fixes, QA checks again only the phases that did not pass and the phases whose own inputs changed since they passed (their files, their tests, or their goal and plan); an untouched phase keeps its pass

rules.text: each QA pass records what the phase's files, tests, and goal and plan were
a phase that never passed or whose last verdict was fail is checked again
a phase that passed and whose files, tests, goal and plan are unchanged is not checked again and keeps its pass (two phases, one touched: only that one is listed)
a changed file alone, a changed test alone, a changed goal alone and a changed plan alone each make a passed phase checked again
a change to a file that belongs to no phase checks no phase
fixes that close without touching any phase file leave all passes standing
a pass that keeps standing still counts as QA passed on the proven code
a record written before this change (passes without digests) is read without error, never called corrupt, and its phases are checked again once
vbw qa record still refuses a proof older than the current code
vbw next gives the narrowed list and the verify workflow checks exactly that list with no selection of its own
a record carrying QA digests is schema 2, so an older VBW says it needs a newer VBW

requirements.text: When QA runs, VBW says for each phase why it is checked again (failed last time, or which of its inputs changed) and lists the phases whose pass still stands

rules.text: each re-checked phase is named with its reason: failed last time, never checked, or which input changed
a phase that builds on a re-checked phase names it
a phase with several reasons shows all of them, and the reasons list is exactly the phases sent to QA
the phases whose pass still stands are listed with their ids
when nothing needs checking again the output says so and lists every phase as standing
the reasons appear in vbw next --json, in the status line file and in vbw show qa text
the wording has no unexplained jargon for a user at level never with plain explanations, in the qa skill too
the docs describe the re-check rule
a real-user scenario shows a fix round followed by QA that checks only the changed phase and names why; it is reported as not run until it is run

requirements.text: A phase is also checked again when a phase it builds on was checked again because its inputs changed, even if its own inputs did not

rules.text: a phase that builds on a re-checked phase is checked again even when its own inputs did not change
the rule is transitive: A, B on A and C on B all re-check
a dependency on a phase that is not re-checked adds nothing
a dependent that never passed is already included and listed once
a dependent is still checked when its changed phase passed again but the dependent's own round was interrupted
a dependency cycle does not hang or crash and is named
a dependency on a missing plan or phase is reported by name

requirements.text: Before planning, VBW asks the user only about decisions for the milestone being planned, never about requirements of shipped milestones

rules.text: the planning step receives only the active milestone's requirements, no shipped one
a requirement carried over to the active milestone counts as active
a requirement with no milestone is reported by name, never silently dropped
a real decision for an active requirement is still asked
a milestone with only technical changes returns no decision and planning goes on without a user round
the decision step still passes a schema and carries the user's level, explanation depth and involvement
planning stops with a clear message when it is not given the requirements

requirements.text: A VBW panel in Claude Code shows, in plain words, the milestone and its progress, what VBW is doing right now (planning, building which parts, checking), and whether it needs the user and for what; it updates by itself within a few seconds when that changes

rules.text: the panel states the milestone and its progress (phases done of total, counting only this milestone's phases whose check passed) in plain sentences
a milestone with no phases says no phases are planned yet, and a single phase is counted in the singular
the panel names what VBW is doing right now: planning, building (naming which parts), checking, fixing or mapping, with minutes so far, and says so when idle
the panel says whether it needs the user and for what (approval, a result to check, a decision, a question), and says nothing is needed when it does not
a question raised for the user is a need, and a need has a stable key that changes when the request changes
every row is a plain sentence with its technical term beside it, and the plain sentence uses no jargon (D107)
a missing, empty or invalid project state gives one neutral line and never throws
the pane draws each term in small dim text beside its sentence and draws only its own pane
after a phase finishes, a run starts, or a need is raised or cleared, the panel shows the new state within 5 seconds with no action by the user
a half-written, missing or invalid project file keeps the last good text, raises no error, and recovers when the file is good again

in a real Claude Code session the panel shows the milestone and progress, what VBW is doing, what it needs from the user, the cost line and an estimate or 'no basis yet' (L3 scenario with a committed result)

requirements.text: The panel opens by itself in a wide window, and at any width with a command; the user can close it, and it stays closed until they open it again

rules.text: a VBW project session opens the panel by itself without taking the keyboard, and where Claude Code keeps it closed (a narrow window) it is not tried again and nothing fails
the /vbw-panel command opens the panel at any width
closing the panel by hand keeps it closed on new activity and in new sessions, until the user opens it again, and that choice is remembered across sessions
only the user's own close is remembered, a close is never refused, and closing another pane changes nothing
opening and closing write no file and change no project data; the choice is kept in the user store, and outside a VBW project the panel is never opened

requirements.text: On Claude Code versions without mods (older than 2.1.287), or outside a VBW project, nothing breaks: no panel and no error, and the status line works as before

rules.text: on Claude Code older than 2.1.287, or with a version that cannot be read, the panel registers no command, starts no timer, opens no pane, reads no file and raises no error
outside a VBW project (no .vbw record, or only a VBW 1 plan) there is no panel, no command and no error
failures of Claude Code's own calls and garbage in the project files never make a hook fail
on 2.1.287 or newer, inside a VBW project, the panel starts
the panel is a mod named by hooks.json 'modules' beside the unchanged hooks, and Claude Code's validator reads its hooks without warnings
the status line output is byte-identical with and without the panel, inside and outside a VBW project, with colour and without, on any Claude Code version

requirements.text: The panel is easy to read at a glance at the user's level
The panel stays light: it uses no network, and its updates do not slow Claude Code down

rules.text: the panel calls nothing that reaches the network, credentials, processes or settings, and reads only files inside the project
the panel never writes: not the record and not any file
when nothing changed no file is read and no redraw is asked for; during a run it redraws only when the shown minute changes
a changed file is read once and drawn once however many ticks follow
the CPU time of a refresh that found nothing and of one that redraws is measured by tools/bench-panel.sh and stays within the stated budget
the budget is enforced: an impossible budget fails the bench, and the budget is stated in docs/panel.md
the panel's code contains no network, credential, process or write call, and never writes the record
the kernel stays within 3,500 lines and the workflows within 1,500 lines, and the panel's tests run in the suite

requirements.text: The panel shows how much the current session has cost so far

rules.text: the cost so far is one small line with its term beside it, with no breakdown
the cost follows the session within 5 seconds
when the cost is not available the line is left out or says not available, never a number or a zero
only read-only calls are made to learn the cost
a refresh that also reads the cost and works out estimates stays within the panel's CPU budget
docs/panel.md says the cost is one line, for this session, and when it is not available

requirements.text: VBW plays a short sound when it needs the user (an approval, a question, a result to check), picked at random from the sounds shipped with VBW in plugin/assets/audio/<character>/; one click in the panel or one command turns it off or on, and the choice is remembered

rules.text: a need for the user plays the sound once, not again while the need stands, and again for the next request or when the same need returns
a question for the user plays the sound once and the need ends when it is answered; other tool calls make no sound
the sound plays even when the panel is closed
the sound is on by default, /vbw-sound switches it off, on or over and says which, and with it off nothing plays for any need
the panel shows whether the sound is on and one click switches it
the choice survives a restart and lives in the user store, never in the project
a missing sound file or no player is silent: nothing plays and nothing is shown
on a version without mods the panel and its sound do nothing and register no command
raising a need and playing the sound costs less than the hook CPU limit of 8 ms, measured
on Claude Code without mods /vbw:panel says plainly that the panel and sound need 2.1.287 or newer, and help and README list the commands
the docs say the sound preference is the user's own and never committed
the plugin ships its sounds in plugin/assets/audio/<character>/ and the sound played is picked at random from them, not from one fixed file

requirements.text: The panel shows an estimated time left for the current step and for the milestone, based on how long earlier steps took in this project, and says plainly when it has no basis for an estimate yet

rules.text: with fewer than 3 finished steps of a kind the step has no basis and no number; the usual time is the median of the last 10 steps of that kind, and other kinds are not counted
a step that runs past its usual time is 'longer', never negative; with no step running there is no step estimate

the milestone estimate is the running step's time left plus phases left times the usual build plus check time, has no basis without enough build and check history, and is nothing when no phase is left
bad history entries are ignored without a crash or a wrong number
ending a run records one finished step (kind, run, start, end, seconds) in the clone's steps.json, oldest first, only the latest 50, shared by worktrees
the history adds no record field, no schema change and no tracked file, and a damaged or unwritable cache never stops a run from ending
a run ended with no run open records nothing
with no or too little history the panel says plainly it has no basis and shows no time; with enough it shows about N min for the step and the milestone
a step past its usual time says it is taking longer than usual and shows no negative time; idle shows only the milestone; no phase left shows no milestone estimate
a missing or garbled history means no history and no error, and in a linked worktree the history is read from its clone
the history is only read, from the clone cache, with no network, and the shown estimate follows the clock
the estimate code is pure and local, states MIN_STEPS = 3, and the panel reads history only from steps.json
a refresh that works out two estimates stays within the panel's CPU budget
docs/panel.md says how many finished steps an estimate needs, that it is approximate, and where the history is kept

requirements.text: The interview opens with: "Hello, Human! Welcome to VBW. Let me interview you real quick to better adapt to you. What is your level of proficiency?", with the same four options as before

rules.text: the first thing the interview says is exactly the new greeting
the four options follow it in the same order and wording
choosing a level still records it and continues the interview
later questions, follow-up rules and keep order are unchanged
the old opening wording is gone from the skill and docs/interview.md, and the docs show the greeting
the router and interview prompt stay within their budgets
a returning user with a recorded level is not asked the level question again

requirements.text: At every stop, VBW ends its message with one plain line saying what it needs from the user now, or that it needs nothing

rules.text: the router tells VBW to end every stop with one line of what it needs from the user, or nothing
the router stays within its 1,400-word budget

requirements.text: Approval is offered as a choice: VBW asks with the options Approve (first, so Enter approves), Not yet (VBW asks what to change) and the user's own words; picking Approve approves exactly the contract shown, recorded by VBW's own code from the user's answer so Claude can never approve by itself; typing /vbw:approve still works

rules.text: the approval question offers Approve first, Not yet second, and the question names the contract by its 12-character fingerprint
approve with a fingerprint approves the contract it names with the same decision entry as plain approve, once per approval whichever path is used
if the contract changed after the question, approving by its old fingerprint approves nothing and says the contract changed
a malformed fingerprint or a contract not ready for approval is refused and nothing is written
answering Approve to VBW's approval question approves exactly the contract the question named, through VBW's own hook
when the contract changed after the question, Approve approves nothing, and the user is told in plain words and shown the new contract
answering Not yet approves nothing and VBW is told to ask what to change
the user's own words approve nothing and are treated as what to change or a question
any other question, in a VBW project or outside one, changes nothing and prints nothing
when the hook cannot approve (nothing ready, already approved, damaged record) nothing changes, the record is untouched and the user sees one sentence saying why and what to do
the decision is recorded once per approval even when both the choice and /vbw:approve are used
the answer may arrive as a map or a list of answers
the model's own call to approve is still refused by the guard
an answer-shaped message from the model, another tool's result, or a subagent does not approve
the new hook stays within the hot-path budget and the kernel within 3,500 lines
the router asks for approval with a choice, Approve first, built from the question the kernel prints, and says what to do with each answer; typing /vbw:approve still works
the prompts stay within their budgets
the docs and the README describe the choice, the Approve-first order and that /vbw:approve still works
a real Claude Code scenario shows the choice appearing and Enter approving the shown contract, and says whether it ran

requirements.text: Once the interview knows what is being built, VBW asks the user's permission to look for the best tools for this project (community skills, automated code-safety scanners, code-quality tools such as linters and formatters, unit-test and other test frameworks); on yes, Scouts research current best-in-class options for the project's stack, with sources, and VBW proposes a short list; nothing is installed until the user approves that list; on no, nothing is searched or installed; it is asked once per project, and /vbw:skills runs it again any time

rules.text: the permission question is asked once the interview knows what is being built, as one plain yes/no question that explains each kind of tool
the question is asked once per project: the answer is remembered in the project record and a second pass does not ask again
the interview skill reads the remembered answer and skips the question when there is one
on no nothing is searched or installed, the record shows no, and the flow continues unchanged
on no the interview skill starts no Scout, searches nothing and installs nothing
on yes a Scout per angle (safety, quality, tests, skills) runs in parallel on the project's own stack
each pick carries a source link; a pick without one is not shown
respected open-source picks are proposed; anything else carries a plain warning
the proposed list is short, trusted picks first
a Scout that fails or finds nothing, or an unknown stack, gives a plain note and no error
the skills skill shows each item in plain words (what, why it fits, where from) and lets the user keep, drop or look further for untrusted picks
nothing is installed until the user approves the list; declining, not yet or a partial approval installs only what was approved
for each approved tool the user is asked project only or all projects and the install goes to that scope
when nothing is found or the stack is unknown the skills skill says so plainly and installs nothing
/vbw:skills runs the research at any time, after a yes or a no, from any state of a VBW project
/vbw:skills can store the answer again later and the record stays valid
the skills skill ends every stop with one plain line saying what VBW needs
the interview step ends with the line 'I need your yes or no to look for tools'
the user documentation explains the offer, trusted sources, approval before install, the scope choice and /vbw:skills
a real Claude Code run shows the answer stored once, not asked again, and nothing installed before approval

requirements.text: The recommended tools fit the project and are explained at the user's level
VBW's own real-app test sessions never play the sound aloud and never read or change the user's own panel and sound choices

rules.text: a VBW test session plays no sound aloud
a VBW test session never reads or changes the user's own panel and sound choices
every real-app test project is marked as a test session, and scenarios read only the test keys

phases.title: Kernel safety: concurrent consent and interrupted commits
phases.goal: The kernel never loses a consent grant and never leaves debris when a command is interrupted.
criteria: A test starts two consent grants at once from two worktrees of one clone, and both grants are in consent.json afterwards.
That test fails on the pre-fix code, and the failure is shown.
A test interrupts a vbw commit mid-way, and .vbw/runtime holds no stray index files afterwards.
A test sets a caller EXIT trap, interrupts the commit, and the caller's trap still runs.

The kernel is still within 3,000 lines.

phases.title: Honest report and rtk commands
phases.goal: vbw report and vbw rtk behave as their --help text says.
criteria: Each claim in the help text of vbw report and vbw rtk has a test that runs the command and checks the stated outcome.
Where the command and its help disagreed, one was corrected, and a regression test fails without that correction.
The help text and the user docs (docs/) say the same thing about both commands.
bash tools/test.sh passes in full.

phases.title: Balanced autonomy: background QA reaches the accept stop
phases.goal: In balanced autonomy, a background QA run ends cleanly and the session reaches the accept stop.
criteria: An L3 scenario in tools/l3-suite.sh runs balanced autonomy with a background QA run on a named fixture.
The session transcript and debug log hold zero Stop-hook errors during that run.
The record shows the session stopped at the accept stop.
The L3 result names its fixture, its cost and its evidence level.

phases.title: Docs agent builds a documentation requirement
phases.goal: A documentation requirement is built by the Docs agent and proved in a real session.
criteria: An L3 scenario drives /vbw:vibe on a fixture whose spec has one documentation requirement.
The record shows the Docs agent built it, by agent type.
The requirement's check is approved and passes in the record, and the commit carries provenance.
The result is logged with fixture, cost and evidence level.

phases.title: QA fails a deviating build and the fix loop closes it
phases.goal: QA fails a phase whose build deviates from its plan, and the fix loop brings it back to passing.
criteria: An L3 scenario seeds a build that deviates from its plan (a named deviation, e.g. a file the plan requires is missing).
The record shows the QA verdict as fail and names that deviation.
The record shows at least one fix iteration, then a QA verdict of pass.
The phase ends proved, and the number of fix rounds is logged.

phases.title: Approval survives blocking and resetting a plan
phases.goal: Blocking or resetting a plan never withdraws the user's approval of a contract whose content is unchanged.
criteria: With an approved contract, setting a plan's note leaves the contract approval in place and the approved hash unchanged
With an approved contract, blocking a plan leaves the approval in place
With an approved contract, resetting a plan's status leaves the approval in place
Changing the contract content (a requirement, check or plan definition) still withdraws the approval
After block or reset on an unchanged contract, the next vbw next --json proceeds without asking for re-approval
Each case has a bats regression test that fails without the fix, and bash tools/test.sh passes under /bin/bash 3.2 and bash 5
The kernel stays within its 3,000-line budget

phases.title: Accept closes only the user's own fixes
phases.goal: Accepting a [human] requirement closes only the fixes opened by the user's own rejections, and leaves QA-opened fixes open until QA passes the phase again.
criteria: Test: a user rejection opens a fix, and a later accept of that requirement closes it.
Test: a fix opened by QA stays open after the user accepts the requirement.
Test: the QA-opened fix closes only when QA records a passing verdict for the phase.
Each regression test fails when run against the code before the fix.
R11 shows as proven in `vbw show requirements`, and bash tools/test.sh passes.

phases.title: QA verdicts require a fresh proof
phases.goal: vbw qa record refuses to record a verdict on a proof older than the current code and tells the caller to run vbw prove first.
criteria: Test: after a code change since the last vbw prove, `vbw qa record` exits non-zero and writes nothing to the record.

phases.title: Run ownership across sessions
phases.goal: A session that does not own the open run is told to wait or check status, and cannot end that run except by the stated exceptions.
criteria: With a run open in session A, `vbw next` in session B reports that the run belongs to another session and advises waiting or `vbw status`; its output contains no instruction to end the run.
`vbw run end` from session B is refused with a non-zero exit and the run stays open in the record.
`vbw run end` from session B succeeds when the user states that the owning session is closed.

phases.title: QA re-checks only phases whose inputs changed, including phases built on them
phases.goal: After a round of fixes, QA checks again only the phases that did not pass, the phases whose own inputs changed since they passed, and the phases that build on a re-checked phase; every other phase keeps its pass.
criteria: Each QA pass stores one digest of the phase's own inputs (its files and tests as committed, its goal and plan, and the digests of the phases it builds on) in the existing qa.tree field; no new record field, the record schema is unchanged (D91); the per-input digests that name a reason are this clone's cache in $(git common dir)/vbw/qa.json
A phase whose last QA verdict was fail or has no pass is checked again.

A phase that passed and whose files, tests, goal and plan are all unchanged is not checked again and keeps its pass (a test with two phases, one touched by a fix, shows only that one in the next QA list).
Changing any one of the three inputs (a file, a test, or the goal or plan) is enough to make a passed phase checked again; each is covered by its own test.
A change to a file that belongs to no phase re-checks no phase.

Dependency rule: a phase that builds on a phase that is re-checked because its inputs changed is also re-checked, even when its own inputs are unchanged; it is transitive (A, then B on A, then C on B all re-check).
Dependency edge: a phase on a re-checked phase that has itself never passed is already included and listed once; a dependency on a phase that is not re-checked adds nothing.
Dependency edge: a cycle or a dependency on a missing phase does not hang or crash; the kernel reports it by name.
Fixes closing without touching any phase files (for example docs outside every phase) leave all passes standing and QA reports nothing to re-check.
vbw qa record on a phase still refuses a proof older than the current code (R12 stays proven).
vbw next and the verify workflow take the narrowed list from the kernel; the workflow holds no selection logic of its own.
Records written before this change (no fingerprint) are read without error and their phases are treated as needing a re-check once; the record is never reported as corrupt (R33, R46 stay proven).
Kernel stays within 3,300 lines and bash 3.2 rules; bats suite passes under /bin/bash and bash 5.

phases.title: A quick test command for build rounds, a full proof for QA and shipping
phases.goal: Build and fix rounds can use a project's faster test command. QA verdicts and shipping are accepted only after a full proof (vbw prove --full) that ran every check and every full project command.
criteria: A project names its quick test command as a Commands entry called `quick` in .vbw/spec.md, for example `- quick: bash tools/test.sh --quick`. It needs approval like any other command. VBW never detects or suggests one (D180), and a project without one behaves as it does today.
When a quick command is named and approved, a plain vbw prove runs it in place of the test command and runs every other project command as before. The test command does not run.
When a quick command is named but not approved, a plain vbw prove runs the full test command instead, so a build round never goes untested. The summary says the quick command was not approved.

vbw prove --full reuses nothing. It runs every approved check, the test command and every other project command, but not the quick command, so nothing runs twice. vbw prove with any other argument is refused with the usage line.

The evidence records whether the proof was full. It is full only when every check and every full project command ran in that proof: none reused, and the quick command not used in place of the test command. A plain vbw prove that happened to run all of them counts as full.
vbw qa record refuses a proof that is not full, without changing the record, and its message says to run vbw prove --full. The existing refusal when the code changed since the proof still applies.
vbw ship refuses a proof that is not full, without changing the record, and its message says to run vbw prove --full.

When the next step would be QA or shipping and the latest proof is not full, vbw next asks for a proof and says to run vbw prove --full (the --json detail marks it as full). The /vbw:vibe router then runs vbw prove --full, so a normal run never reaches a refusal.

The QA agent's and the verifying workflow's instruction for a refused verdict says to run vbw prove --full, then try the record once more. The test-command result given to QA agents comes from the full proof's test command, never from the quick command.
The vbw prove summary says whether the proof was full or partial.

VBW's own project follows D179: tools/test.sh has a quick mode that runs shellcheck, the engineering rules and the core test files, but not the files approved checks already run and not the timing benchmarks. VBW's spec names that mode as its `quick` command.
docs/proof.md and the user docs explain the quick command, when a full proof is needed, and the two refusal messages.
Tests cover each case above, including a project without a quick command, an unapproved quick command, and a refusal followed by a successful vbw prove --full and record.

qa-inputs.sh: qa_digests can fingerprint the phases as they were at a given commit (files and check files from that commit's tree, goal, plans and requirements from that commit's .vbw/record.json), with the current method

When a passed phase's stored fingerprint has another version or none: find the pass's commit (the cache entry's commit, else the earliest commit whose .vbw/record.json holds this phase's current qa entry, same tree and time), fingerprint the phase there with the current method and compare with now. The same means the pass stands; a difference gives the usual reasons (its files, tests, goal or plan, an [auto] requirement, a phase it builds on); no such commit means it is checked again as today. The result goes back into the clone's cache at the current version, so the history is read once per pass

plugin/lib/qa.jq and its callers (qa_state in cmd-next.sh, the phase view's `[on older code]` mark in cmd-show.sh, cmd-qa.sh when it records a pass) use that one judgment; at the same version a different fingerprint is still a change, read straight from the digests as today

plans.title: tools/test.sh can run one share of the suite
tasks: Arguments: `--shard K/N` and `--shard K/N --list`, K and N whole numbers with 1 <= K <= N. Anything else (0, K above N, not a number, a missing or extra argument, --list first) prints `usage: tools/test.sh [--quick [--list]] | --shard K/N [--list]` and exits 2 before running anything. The no-argument run and --quick keep exactly their current behaviour (tests/quick-mode.bats keeps passing)

Shares: computed at run time from tests/*.bats, by test count (the number of `@test` lines): files sorted from most tests to fewest (ties by name), each given to the shard with the fewest tests so far (ties to the lowest number). Same files give the same shares; every file lands in exactly one shard; no list of files to maintain

A shard run: shard 1 alone runs the shellcheck lint of tools/*.sh, tools/bench-hooks.sh and, when node exists, tools/bench-panel.sh, as the full run does. Every shard runs its ordinary files in one `bats --print-output-on-failure --jobs J` batch (J = half the cores, as today), then its timed files (prove-parallel, guard-cost, bench-hooks, proof-stale-links, in that order) with plain `bats --print-output-on-failure`; an empty group is skipped; any failure makes the script exit non-zero

`--shard K/N --list` prints what shard K would run, one line each, and runs nothing: for shard 1 first the stages `shellcheck tools/*.sh`, `bash tools/bench-hooks.sh`, `bash tools/bench-panel.sh`, then the batch files, then the timed files. The timed-file list is written once and shared by the full, quick and shard runs

BASE empty, all zeros, not a commit in this clone, or not an ancestor of HEAD (new branch, rewritten history, shallow clone): full suite, with that reason

Changed files: `git diff --name-status -z -M BASE HEAD` (NUL-separated, as the project's git rule asks), which covers every commit of the push. A renamed or copied file is sorted under its new path and its old path too (a file moved out of plugin/ still counts as a plugin change); a deleted file is sorted but never run

Output, three lines ready for GitHub's step outputs: `scope=full|some|none`, `files=` (the test files to run, sorted, space-separated; empty unless some) and `reason=` in plain words (the first path that forced the full suite, the test files, or 'only the VBW record or saved test results changed'); a push that only deletes test files gives none

Parallel proof can break the check gate under load. plugin/lib/checks.sh line 102 creates the lock owner file with printf > $g/mutex/pid right after mkdir; a waiting check that reads that file while it is still empty treats the owner as dead and runs rm -rf on a live lock (the gate's takeover test passes an empty pid to checks_gate_live). Parallel proof makes this window common. The Linux suite already hit it (mutex/pid: No such file or directory). Evidence: tests/gate-race.bats (untracked, not committed) fails 2 of 3 on HEAD: 'a lock whose owner file reads empty is not taken over at once' (the check took the lock: C1 pass 0s) and 'the owner write never prints an error' (checks.sh:102 matches). Fix: do not take over on an empty owner file until a wait has passed, write the owner file so a vanished lock prints nothing, commit the test. decisions.text: QA re-check data adds no new record field and no schema change: a phase's QA pass stores one digest of that phase's own inputs (its plans' files, its checks' files, its goal, criteria, plans and rules, and the digests of phases it builds on) in the existing qa.tree field; the per-input digests used to name a reason are a clone-local cache in $(git common dir)/vbw/qa.json; without the cache the reason is 'its inputs changed'

top.text: Skip the second full check run after a fix that only changes documentation. Today, if QA (VBW's final review) finds a problem and the fix only edits documentation, VBW still reruns its whole test suite, about 23 minutes on VBW itself, before QA looks again. With this change, VBW reuses the earlier test results when only documentation has changed since they ran, the same way QA already does under R115.
top.reason: Decision D220 already named this as the next pick once M18 shipped, and M18 has now shipped (D222); it is a small change that saves about 23 minutes each time it applies.

runners.text: Fix a QA depth bug. A phase that was raised to the strictest review level ('deep') is currently reviewed at the lighter 'standard' level, because a small-change shortcut still applies to it. This happened to P89, P90 and P92, and P92 failed QA four times. A phase that was raised should keep the review level it was given.

Backlog commands (vbw todo add, sort, done and drop) leave the project record file unsaved in git when they are the last command run. Have them commit it, as vbw recommend has done since 2.0.29, without touching any files the user has staged.
